correctness.rationale: Schoenberg Gram reduction is exact; the arm-difference block is positive definite by the displayed integral for 1<p<2. The branch-constant block has a unique one-dimensional determinant crossing before the ordinary-star threshold, proved by strict derivative signs and concavity; outside the interval it violates positive semidefiniteness. The endpoint nullity and m-decrease follow from rank and strict Loewner comparison, and a uniform 1/m expansion proves the coefficient. Finite code checks independently reconstruct graph distances, the block entries and critical roots, but universal proof is analytic.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Sanchez gives a test for any finite metric, so the present family is algorithmically in its scope, but there is no stated root, monotonicity, endpoint eigenvector or uniform asymptotic; reducing that test and proving the sharp comparison are substantive new steps. Doust-Weston gives only the unsubdivided star value and general lower bounds. Li-Weston supplies only strictness and interval consequences.
